clue.text: Roll on strike meeting!

parts.note: to roll over is to turn
workers on strike are out

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for a union meeting that will vote to roll on with the strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll on' reads as a cheer of 'bring it on', but the words split into two pieces, and 'meeting' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The turnout is the gathering of people who attend an event, so it stands for a meeting.

clue.text: The Italian leader involved in deals gets much abuse

indicators.note: involved in means the leading letter is placed inside the dealing word

parts.note: trades are deals

indicators.note: the leader of Italian is its first letter

explanation.surface: An Italian chief dealing shadily earns plenty of criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' is only a link; 'leader' takes I from Italian, set inside TRADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, a stream of verbal abuse.

clue.text: Restore control on political power

parts.note: a rein is a means of control
the state is the political power of a nation

explanation.surface: Bring back control over the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to put back into a former position.

clue.text: Light-weight union leader at one point imprisoned

indicators.note: imprisoned means the union's first letter is shut inside the other piece

parts.note: once means at one point in time

indicators.note: the leader of union is its first letter

explanation.surface: A slight union boss was jailed for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light-weight' suggests a feeble person, but means a small unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is a small unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: To follow only a fraction is just the end!

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them
a piece is a fraction of a whole

explanation.surface: A complaint that following only part is the limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only' and 'is just' are links; the exclamation is a tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is a final section added at the end of a book or work.

clue.text: Elderly lady in complete flutter

parts.note: to do a job is to complete it
a flutter is a small bet, a British term

explanation.surface: An old woman in a state of total excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' looks like agitation, but in Britain a flutter is a small bet on a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically an older woman.

clue.text: One who administers drug to performer receiving money

indicators.note: receiving means the performer takes the money into its middle

parts.note: a doer is one who performs
p, a penny, is British money

explanation.surface: Someone drugs an entertainer who is being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doper gives stimulants illegally, for instance to racehorses.

clue.text: Force to dive under the lake

indicators.note: in a down answer, under means the second piece comes below the first

parts.note: a lake is a body of water
to dive is to fall

explanation.surface: Being made to plunge beneath the lake's surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Force is a northern English word for a waterfall, as in the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England a force is a cascade, from the Norse word for one.

clue.text: In a tangle — a mess — one has to be bright

indicators.note: In tells the solver the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone in a hopeless muddle still has to look cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'a' and 'one has to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To gleam is to shine or glow with light.

clue.text: Gunmen appear above suspicion in such competitive activity

indicators.note: appear above means in this down answer the first piece is placed on top

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners
a trace is a suspicion, a tiny amount

explanation.surface: Armed men turn up above suspicion in a cut-throat business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'above suspicion' reads as innocent, but 'appear above' places RA over TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the ruthless struggle for success in working life.

clue.text: Concerned with private US backing, point to rule

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: backing means the soldier's letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: a GI is a private soldier in the US army
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Someone involved with an American soldier's support aims to govern.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is the period or act of ruling a country.

clue.text: In time apt perhaps to get irritable

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Someone usually punctual grows cross when kept waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals rearranging the nine letters of IN TIME APT; 'to get' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An impatient person is easily annoyed by delay, close to being short-tempered.

clue.text: Colourful stuff giving rise to complaint

explanation.surface: Some paint brings on an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' is only a link between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is a cheap wall paint coloured with pigment, and also a viral illness of dogs.

clue.text: Music that's off-beat to some degree

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A tune that is somewhat syncopated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off-beat' suggests rhythm, but here it means strange: RUM in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban dance, and the dance tune played for it.

clue.text: Skinhead thanks representative to create an impression

parts.note: the head of the word skin is its first letter
ta is British informal for thank you
an MP, Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A thug in boots gratefully asks his MP to make a mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinhead reads as a thug, but splits as the head of 'skin', its first letter S; 'to create an' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stamp is a mark pressed into a surface, an impression left by a die.

clue.text: Limiting factor that's normal with a measuring device

parts.note: par is the normal standard
a meter measures things like gas or water

explanation.surface: A constraint that is quite ordinary with a gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a boundary or condition that sets limits on something.

clue.text: Put out over change of diet

parts.note: in cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat, also called a sundry; here over gives extra as in left over

indicators.note: a change of the word diet means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushed aside over a new eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an extra is a run not scored off the bat; 'change of' rearranges the eating word into DITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to send a suspect out of one country to face trial in another.

clue.text: This registers the main rises and falls

definitions.text: This registers the main rises and falls

parts.words: This registers the main rises and falls
parts.note: the main is the sea, and its rising and falling are recorded in a printed schedule

explanation.surface: Something that records the principal ups and downs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is old poetic language for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a published list gives times of high and low water for a harbour.

clue.text: Emphasise it, a pest is to be put inside

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to be put inside means the small word goes within the pest

parts.note: lice are a pest, taken collectively
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stress that a nuisance is to be jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put inside' sounds like going to prison, but it is a container signal; lice counts as one pest collectively.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type is used in print to stress a word.

clue.text: Front men to start a charge

explanation.surface: Soldiers in the vanguard lead the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The spearhead is the leading group of an assault, and to spearhead is to lead an attack.

clue.text: A composer making his mark?

parts.note: one who makes a mark or blot shares a name with the Victorian church composer John

explanation.surface: A musician becoming famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer wrote church music, and one who leaves marks is literally a marker of blots.

clue.text: See the short answer in borrowed money

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
ans is a short form of answer

explanation.surface: Look up the brief reply about money lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Loans are sums lent which the recipient must repay.

clue.text: Having no boy to disrupt lessons

indicators.note: to disrupt the word lessons is to break its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Childless parents interrupting classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A man without male children is without a male heir.

clue.text: At the side of a supporter

parts.note: a beam supports a roof or floor

explanation.surface: Standing beside someone who backs you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam is a nautical term for at right angles to a ship's keel, off its side.

clue.text: Several dined soundly

indicators.note: soundly means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: ate means dined

explanation.surface: A few people ate well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soundly' looks like 'well', but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight is a number, one of many quantities that count as a handful.

clue.text: State whereabouts

explanation.surface: A request to give your current location.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation is a state of affairs, and also the place where something is located.

clue.text: Substantial cover provided beforehand

indicators.note: beforehand means the first piece goes before the other

parts.note: so means provided that
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Insurance cover arranged in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid is firm and sturdy rather than flimsy.

clue.text: Make sense of tot

explanation.surface: Understand a sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts that add up are coherent, and to add up is to total figures.

clue.text: Unusual thing, wallop, to find in such a place of entertainment!

indicators.note: unusual means the word thing is arranged unconventionally

parts.note: to club someone is to hit them hard

explanation.surface: A strange object and a blow to be met at a venue for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges THING into NIGHT; 'to find in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub is a venue open late with music, drinks and dancing.

clue.text: Be pushed into a private road

definitions.text: Be pushed into a private road

parts.words: Be pushed into a private road
parts.note: to be pushed is to be ..., and a private road leading to a house shares the same name

explanation.surface: Being forced down someone's own approach road.
explanation.definitionFit: A driveway is a private road to a house, and to push or impel is another sense of the word.

clue.text: Went back and finished work

explanation.surface: Someone left after their career ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To have retired is to have withdrawn backwards, and also to have stopped working for good.

clue.text: Superseded newsmen, say

parts.note: ex means former, superseded
the press are journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Journalists who have been replaced, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words.
